metadata.description: Medical insights knowledge base with personalization support

rules.insight: Low hemoglobin levels can be associated with anemia, which may result from iron deficiency, vitamin deficiencies, or other factors. Consult a healthcare provider for proper evaluation.

age_variants.pediatric: Low hemoglobin in children may indicate iron deficiency anemia, which is common during growth spurts. A healthcare provider can assess nutritional needs.
age_variants.geriatric: Low hemoglobin in older adults may be related to chronic disease, nutritional deficiencies, or bone marrow changes. Medical evaluation is recommended.

diet: Increase iron-rich foods (red meat, spinach, lentils)
Pair iron sources with vitamin C for better absorption
supplements: Iron supplementation may be recommended by your doctor
Take iron supplements on an empty stomach if tolerated
monitoring: Regular follow-up blood tests to track improvement

symptom_questions: Are you experiencing unusual fatigue or weakness?
Have you noticed pale skin or shortness of breath?
Do you have heavy menstrual periods? (for females)

rules.insight: Elevated hemoglobin levels can occur due to dehydration, smoking, living at high altitudes, or other underlying conditions. Using this result for self-diagnosis is not recommended.

hydration: Ensure adequate daily water intake (8-10 glasses)
Increase fluids during exercise or hot weather
smoking: If you smoke, consider cessation programs
monitoring: Track symptoms like headaches or dizziness

symptom_questions: Have you been adequately hydrated?
Do you smoke or use tobacco products?
Do you live at high altitude?

rules.insight: A high white blood cell count (Leukocytosis) is often a sign of the body reacting to an infection or inflammation, but can have other causes.

rest: Get adequate sleep and rest to support immune function
hygiene: Practice good hygiene to prevent infections

symptom_questions: Have you had recent infections or illness?
Are you experiencing fever or chills?
Have you been under significant stress?

rules.insight: A low white blood cell count (Leukopenia) can be seen in various conditions, including viral infections or bone marrow issues. Medical advice is recommended.

prevention: Avoid crowded places during flu season
diet: Eat a balanced diet rich in vitamins and minerals
Consider vitamin B12 and folate sources
precautions: Report any signs of infection immediately to your doctor

symptom_questions: Have you had recent viral infections?
Are you taking any new medications?
Do you have frequent infections?

rules.insight: Low platelet count (Thrombocytopenia) may affect blood clotting. Common causes include viral infections, nutrient deficiencies, or medication side effects.

safety: Avoid contact sports and activities with injury risk
Use soft toothbrush to prevent gum bleeding
diet: Ensure adequate vitamin B12 and folate intake
precautions: Report unusual bruising or bleeding immediately

symptom_questions: Have you noticed unusual bruising or bleeding?
Do you have frequent nosebleeds?
Are you taking any blood-thinning medications?

rules.insight: High platelet count (Thrombocytosis) can satisfy a normal reaction to inflammation or infection, but persistent elevation should be evaluated by a doctor.

hydration: Stay well-hydrated to maintain blood flow
monitoring: Follow up with your healthcare provider

symptom_questions: Have you had recent infections or surgery?
Do you experience headaches or dizziness?

rules.insight: Elevated fasting glucose levels can be associated with insulin resistance, pre-diabetes, or diabetes mellitus. Lifestyle modification and medical consultation are recommended.

diet: Reduce refined carbohydrates and sugary foods
Choose whole grains over white bread/rice
exercise: Aim for 150 minutes of moderate exercise weekly
Include both cardio and strength training
weight: If overweight, even 5-10% weight loss can improve blood sugar
monitoring: Check blood sugar regularly as recommended

symptom_questions: Do you experience increased thirst or urination?
Have you noticed unexplained weight loss?
Do you feel unusually tired?

rules.insight: Low fasting glucose (hypoglycemia) may be caused by medication, prolonged fasting, or hormonal imbalances. Please discuss with your healthcare provider.

monitoring: Track when symptoms occur in relation to meals
precautions: Carry a quick sugar source (glucose tablets, juice)

symptom_questions: Do you experience shakiness, sweating, or confusion?
Do symptoms improve after eating?
Are you taking diabetes medications?

rules.insight: Elevated HbA1C indicates poor long-term blood sugar control and may suggest pre-diabetes or diabetes. This marker reflects average glucose levels over the past 2-3 months.

diet: Follow a low glycemic index diet
Limit processed foods and added sugars
Eat balanced meals with protein, fiber, healthy fats
exercise: Regular physical activity improves insulin sensitivity
weight: Weight loss can significantly improve HbA1C levels
sleep: Aim for 7-9 hours of quality sleep
Poor sleep affects blood sugar control

symptom_questions: Have you been monitoring your blood sugar at home?
Are you following a diabetes meal plan?
How has your energy level been?

rules.insight: Elevated total cholesterol is a risk factor for cardiovascular disease. Lifestyle modifications including diet and exercise, along with medical guidance, are recommended.

exercise: Aim for 150 minutes moderate aerobic activity weekly
smoking: Quit smoking to improve HDL levels

symptom_questions: Do you have a family history of high cholesterol or heart disease?
What does your typical diet look like?
How often do you exercise?

rules.insight: Elevated LDL (bad cholesterol) is a major risk factor for atherosclerosis and cardiovascular disease. Diet, exercise, and possibly medication may be recommended.

diet: Limit saturated fat to <7% of calories
Add nuts and seeds in moderation
exercise: Regular aerobic exercise can lower LDL
weight: Even modest weight loss helps reduce LDL

symptom_questions: Do you have chest pain or shortness of breath?
What is your family cardiac history?

rules.insight: Low HDL (good cholesterol) is a risk factor for heart disease. Regular exercise and healthy fats can help increase HDL levels.

exercise: Aerobic exercise is most effective for raising HDL
Aim for at least 30 minutes 5 days/week
diet: Include healthy fats (olive oil, avocados, nuts)
smoking: Quitting smoking can raise HDL by up to 10%
alcohol: Moderate alcohol may raise HDL (consult your doctor)

symptom_questions: Do you exercise regularly?
Do you smoke?
What does your typical diet include?

rules.insight: Elevated triglycerides increase cardiovascular risk and can be associated with obesity, diabetes, or metabolic syndrome. Dietary changes and weight loss may help.

alcohol: Limit or avoid alcohol - it significantly raises triglycerides
exercise: Regular physical activity can lower triglycerides by 20-30%
weight: Weight loss is very effective for lowering triglycerides

symptom_questions: How much alcohol do you consume weekly?
Do you eat a lot of sweets or processed foods?

rules.insight: Elevated TSH indicates hypothyroidism (underactive thyroid). The pituitary gland increases TSH to stimulate the thyroid. Thyroid hormone replacement may be needed.

age_variants.geriatric: Hypothyroidism is common in older adults. Symptoms may be subtle and include fatigue, cold intolerance, and cognitive changes.

diet: Ensure adequate iodine intake (but don't over-supplement)
Selenium-rich foods may support thyroid health
medication: Take thyroid medication on empty stomach
monitoring: Regular TSH monitoring needed to adjust medication

symptom_questions: Are you experiencing fatigue, weight gain, or cold intolerance?
Have you noticed dry skin or hair loss?
Are you feeling depressed or sluggish?

rules.insight: Low TSH can indicate hyperthyroidism (overactive thyroid) or excessive thyroid hormone replacement. The pituitary reduces TSH when thyroid hormone levels are high.

stress: Manage stress - it can affect thyroid function

symptom_questions: Have you experienced rapid heartbeat or palpitations?
Are you losing weight unintentionally?
Do you feel anxious or jittery?
Are you taking thyroid medication?

rules.insight: Elevated creatinine levels may indicate reduced kidney function or dehydration. This is an important marker for kidney health and warrants medical evaluation.

hydration: Ensure adequate fluid intake unless restricted
diet: May need to limit protein intake (consult doctor)
Limit phosphorus if kidney disease confirmed
medications: Avoid NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) - can harm kidneys
blood_pressure: Control blood pressure to protect kidneys

symptom_questions: Are you urinating less frequently?
Do you have swelling in legs or ankles?
Are you experiencing fatigue or confusion?

rules.insight: Elevated BUN (Blood Urea Nitrogen) can indicate reduced kidney function, dehydration, high protein diet, or other conditions. Follow up with your healthcare provider.

diet: May need to moderate protein intake

symptom_questions: Have you been adequately hydrated?
Are you eating a very high protein diet?
Do you have any urinary symptoms?

rules.insight: Vitamin D deficiency can affect bone health, immune function, and overall well-being. Supplementation and sun exposure may be recommended.

sunlight: Get 10-30 minutes of midday sun several times weekly (with sun safety)
Sun exposure is best source of vitamin D
diet: Eat vitamin D-rich foods (fatty fish, egg yolks, fortified milk)
Consider fortified cereals and orange juice
supplements: Your doctor may recommend 1000-2000 IU daily
Take with food containing fat for better absorption
bone_health: Ensure adequate calcium intake (works with vitamin D)

symptom_questions: Do you spend most time indoors?
Are you experiencing bone or muscle pain?
Do you have frequent infections?

rules.insight: Vitamin B12 deficiency can cause anemia, neurological symptoms, and fatigue. Common in vegetarians, elderly, or those with absorption issues. Supplementation is often effective.

age_variants.geriatric: B12 absorption decreases with age. Older adults may need B12 supplements or injections even with adequate dietary intake.

diet: Increase B12-rich foods (meat, fish, dairy, eggs)
Vegetarians: use fortified foods or supplements
Consider fortified nutritional yeast, plant milks
supplements: Injections may be needed if absorption is impaired

symptom_questions: Are you vegetarian or vegan?
Do you experience numbness or tingling in hands/feet?
Have you noticed memory problems or confusion?
Do you feel weak or tired?

rules.insight: Elevated SGPT (ALT) is more specific to liver damage and can be caused by hepatitis, fatty liver disease, medications, or alcohol use.

diet: Reduce saturated fats and refined carbs
Avoid excessive fructose and added sugars
weight: Weight loss can improve fatty liver disease
exercise: Regular physical activity improves liver health
medications: Review all medications and supplements with doctor

symptom_questions: Do you drink alcohol regularly?
Are you taking any new medications or supplements?
Have you experienced jaundice or abdominal pain?

rules.insight: Elevated SGOT (AST) can indicate liver damage, muscle injury, or heart problems. Further evaluation is needed to determine the cause.

exercise: Intense exercise can temporarily elevate AST

symptom_questions: Have you recently done intense physical activity?
Do you have any chest pain or discomfort?
Are you experiencing liver-related symptoms?

rules.insight: Elevated uric acid (Hyperuricemia) can be associated with gout, kidney stones, or kidney disease. Dietary modifications may be recommended.

diet: Limit high-purine foods (red meat, organ meats, certain seafood)
Limit high-fructose corn syrup and sugary drinks
Drink cherry juice (may help lower uric acid)
hydration: Drink plenty of water (helps flush uric acid)
weight: Gradual weight loss can reduce uric acid
Avoid crash diets (can temporarily raise levels)
coffee: Moderate coffee intake may lower uric acid levels

symptom_questions: Have you experienced joint pain, especially in big toe?
Do you have a history of gout attacks?
Have you had kidney stones?
